# Tips from past games

Written 2026-10-10 13:01 by opus-5.5 with `uv run tips.py build`, from the 179 active entries of tips_notebook.json (20 games). Players never see this preamble; they see every section below. Earlier sheets are in history/.

## Everyone
- A visit shows a destination, not an action: tracks and watches can't tell protection from framing or a Katana hit. A corroborated Lookout's lone other visitor to a victim is near-proof; don't let the 'Lookout can't see himself' caveat acquit a repeat visitor. (seen in 12 games)
- Keep votes consistent with your stated reads, and explain any change before voting. A read/vote mismatch is a lead to check against claims and results, never a reason to hang or shoot alone. (seen in 10 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction in claims, votes or mechanical results. Remember a contradiction alone doesn't separate a Yakuza from a Jester who wants the hang. (seen in 10 games)
- Get the mechanics right before calling a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat, unless a full role census plus flips proves a role exists exactly once. (seen in 9 games)
- Write each night's planned target and all results into your will, labelled as plans, so your death still yields information. (seen in 7 games)

## Village
- Map early PM clusters and co-nominations; a group that DMs then pushes together is a likely bloc. Require votes or a mechanical result before hanging on a PM link, since Jesters and Executioners also leave PM trails. (seen in 14 games)
- After a Yakuza flips, top suspects are those who voted No on their nomination, voted Innocent when it could have saved them, or PM'd them. A Guilty vote clears no one. (seen in 12 games)
- Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises far above awkward wording. Before a hang, ask what separates a lie from a mistake, a frame, a Roleplayer or a Jester. (seen in 12 games)
- Don't hint at your power role on Day 1. While a Ritualist may live, never name a living player's exact role in public or in your will. (seen in 12 games)
- Keep Serial Killers and Arsonists in the pool after Yakuza die; a Not Evil read or Vanilla claim doesn't clear them, and a failed kill can mean innate Defense. (seen in 8 games)
- A power-role claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real. (seen in 8 games)
- Investigators and Medics: never announce tonight's target publicly or by PM; it tells the Pharmacist whom to block and the Katana where to strike. (seen in 6 games)
- Once an archive or survey list is public, do slot math daily; a claim that duplicates a once-listed role or overflows unseen slots marks a liar. (seen in 5 games)
- If an announced trial total exceeds the revealed votes, a Ballot Stuffer exists among the voters on the larger side; pick them out by stance/ballot mismatch. (seen in 4 games)
- If the nominee may be a Jester, prefer not hanging; if you must, agree on a bare Guilty majority and keep confirmed power roles off the Guilty side. (seen in 4 games)

## Yakuza
- Bus a doomed teammate with Yes and Guilty. But first do the vote math in night chat: if your Innocents (plus a doubled vote) can save them, defend them. Futile lone Innocents hang you later. (seen in 15 games)
- Fake-claim only a role whose token count matches yours and that no living holder, Lookout or Tracker can contradict; never report more results than its tokens allow. (seen in 11 games)
- Never put team plans in daytime PMs and don't PM teammates on Day 1; Eavesdroppers and Wiretaps read them, and PM triangles become the town's case. (seen in 10 games)
- After a failed Katana, assume protection or innate Defense: kill or block the protector, or hang the survivor, rather than retrying blindly. (seen in 9 games)
- Give the Katana to a low-value member with a cover story ready, and move it the same night a Lookout or Tracker names the holder. (seen in 7 games)
- Every member submits the agreed holder, target and actions every night; with two alive, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 6 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit that could have been seen; agree a cover action in night chat and admit it at once. (seen in 5 games)
- Spend one-shot tokens (rig, puppet, clean) on a decisive day; a dead Yakuza's unused token is wasted. (seen in 4 games)

## Neutral
- If innate Defense saves you, deny being attacked or pick one consistent claim at once; switching claims under pressure gets you hanged. (seen in 3 games)

## Sheriff
- Post every target and result in your first speech after getting it, and counterclaim at once with your full log if someone copies your role. (seen in 8 games)
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil that night, so a Not Evil result clears nothing; say so when posting, and in the endgame rely on votes instead. (seen in 13 games)

## Medic
- Protect likely Katana targets, analysts then claimed investigators. Once you've claimed Medic, self-protect with a token instead of repeating a predictable protection. (seen in 11 games)
- You get no save feedback; say the target's survival is consistent with your protection, never that you confirmed a save. (seen in 4 games)

## Vigilante
- Shoot only on a mechanical lead (claim conflict, Evil check against an unverifiable claim, flipped teammate's links), never a soft read; a hidden Cardinal costs two Good lives. Use Basic shots. (seen in 6 games)

## Clerk
- Rig on a set night for a non-teammate who can pass a nomination but not a Guilty vote; never when a teammate is the likely nominee, and don't hoard it. (seen in 4 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3+ living players are doused or the moment you're suspected; Arsonists who kept dousing were hanged with no kills. (seen in 3 games)

Give Yakuza a team-visible reminder of living members, token counts and the current Katana holder at the start of each night. Make the revealed night summaries say whether a protection or role-block was used, so players can separate a failed attack from a blocked one. Spell out in R23 how a watched visit moves under a swap, with a worked example. Consider a short public note when a will is forged, or a clearer rule that forged wills are invisible to everyone.

answers.confusing_rules: R22 budget is hard to plan from: the prompt gives per-round earnings, a carryover rule and a message-price formula, but I never saw my exact remaining budget or the price of my next message in a single place, so I couldn't judge how long a speech could be. The Katana rules are also easy to misread: 'passing the Katana is not a visit' and the holder's visit only counts for role-blocks and Trackers, so it took several reads to see who could be the attacker. Swap rules (R23) and the Seer's random pair (alive at start of night, including those who die) were clear once spelled out but took effort to apply to a night with deaths.
answers.missing_information: A per-game record of each living player's remaining tokens (Medic, Seer, Fabricator, Vigilante, Smuggler) would have helped me test claims such as a Medic's protections or a Vigilante's shots. I also had no record of who held the Katana at the start of each night without reconstructing it from the public Katana-passing messages. Private message counts were shown only as 'none yet', so I couldn't tell whether any Yakuza were coordinating in the day.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to privately ask Heidi, Grace and Niaj for their exact night targets and results to cross-check them before the vote, but I never sent a private message, and I wasn't sure whether the cheaper private price was worth it given my budget. I also wanted to see how other players' budgets were running out so I could judge who might stop speaking, which the interface didn't show.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: The Yakuza night-chat transcripts and the 'Katana vote' lines appear in the general game log with the night actions, which makes it look as if they were public while the game was still running; I'm not sure whether that's intended as a reveal. The notepad fills up quickly with 12 players, so I had to drop older reads. The Day 2 summary said 'Frank starts' and Day 4 said 'Frank starts' again, which is correct but could confuse players about whether the order rotates.
answers.suggestions: Show the current budget, the price of a short and a long message, and the trial-only budget on each turn. Show the Katana holder publicly each night when it passes, and list each role's remaining token count in the public ledger for dead and living players. Allow a longer notepad or a structured notepad format, since 400 words is tight for 12 players. Clarify in the rules whether dead players' votes still matter for thresholds, and when a Medic's protection is revealed, if ever.

answers.confusing_rules: R19 says alignment checks see a player's “true alignment, except” for effects like framing and holding the Katana. It would be clearer to call these the alignment reported by a check, since they can differ from true alignment. R20 also says role-blocked actions are removed first, then says swaps apply “before anything else”; clarify that this means before resolving remaining actions, not before role-blocking.
answers.missing_information: The information was available, but the long event history made it difficult to keep selected targets, redirected targets, actual visits, and reported alignment results straight. A compact per-night summary distinguishing those would help. I also received my N3 Seer result just before dying, with no opportunity to add it to my will, so that result was not passed on.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I would have liked to record my N3 result in my will after receiving it. The rules only let me update my will during the Day, and I died before I could do so.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: No definite mechanical bug stood out. It was odd that the final private Seer result was delivered to me even though I died that same night and could not communicate it.
answers.suggestions: Clarify the wording and ordering in R19 and R20. Provide a concise night report separating chosen target, redirected destination, visit, and investigation result. Consider allowing a last-will update after night results are delivered, or automatically appending those results to the will if the player dies before the next Day.

answers.confusing_rules: R19’s phrase “true alignment, except” is easy to misread: Sheriff and Seer results can reflect a frame or Katana-holder exception rather than the target’s actual faction. It would be clearer to call these “reported alignment” results and list the exceptions right beside each investigative role. The swap rules also take effort to apply mentally: an action lands on the swapped player, but its result names the player the investigator chose.
answers.missing_information: I wanted a reliable, compact record of public claims, night results, flips, and votes that stayed visible throughout play. I used the notepad for this, but it had to be maintained manually. For interpreting Sheriff results, I also wanted to know whether my chosen target had been redirected; that information may be intentionally withheld, but its absence makes results harder to evaluate.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I had no essential action that the interface prevented. I would have liked a structured way to compare my results against the public record and flag possible frames or swaps without repeatedly restating the same explanation in chat.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: No definite gameplay error stood out in this game. One rules-text inconsistency: R20 says to remove role-blocked actions first, then says swaps apply “before anything else.” Clarify which happens first, since swaps can redirect actions. The R20 checklist could also explicitly place the Cardinal’s delayed attack in the night-resolution order.
answers.suggestions: Provide a persistent public timeline or board showing deaths and flips, claims and corrections, investigation claims, and nomination/trial votes. Make modified alignment results explicit in role instructions and result messages (for example, “appears Evil tonight; this is not necessarily their true alignment”). Reconcile the swap/role-block order in R20 and include all special delayed effects in its checklist.

answers.confusing_rules: The Ex-Con's random visit versus Night 2 Katana attacks was hard to reason about: a random Ex-Con visit can land on a Katana victim by coincidence, so a Lookout's visitor list can't tell the two apart. The Sheriff reading of Katana holders as Good that night, and how an Ex-Con reads as Evil, interacted in ways that took effort to check. Rules about whether a dead player's Katana pass happens after the night's results and whether a Smuggler swap shows as a visit were also easy to misread. The instructions asking to leave reason and feedback empty conflict with the schema's required fields, which was ambiguous (I left them empty as told).
answers.missing_information: I had no running record of who visited whom beyond what the Lookout reported, and no way to see other players' remaining tokens or budgets during the game. The public ledger didn't track speaking budget left per player, so it was hard to judge how much each player could still say. I couldn't see the Yakuza night chat history in a compact form, so keeping my own notes on what teammates had already agreed was error-prone. The private message counts were recorded as none, so I couldn't tell whether any Day 1 PMs happened or were hidden.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: As a Yakuza I wanted a private way to agree a cover story with Carol or Erin during the day without creating a PM trail, and no such channel existed except public chat. I wanted to ask the moderator for a neutral summary of my teammates' visible actions, which isn't available. I also wanted to check whether a Sheriff's Not Evil result on a Katana holder could be verified against the Katana state, but that information isn't given to the player.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing clearly broke, but the Night 3 private summary told Erin she had 2 swap tokens and recorded her night actions even though she was killed that same night by the Vigilante, which is consistent with simultaneous resolution but looked odd. The Katana holder being announced as passing at the start of Day 3 after Ivan's execution, while Ivan's last will still claimed Ex-Con, was consistent but made the cause of Katana transfers hard to follow. The moderator summaries repeated Katana holder and target lines in several places, which was redundant.
answers.suggestions: Show a running public list of each player's remaining tokens where tokens are public (such as Medic and Sheriff), and show each living player's remaining speaking budget at the start of each Day. Add a short per-night public ledger of which roles were blocked or visited, if the rules allow it. Clarify in the prompt that reason and feedback may be left empty and whether lessons and tips_feedback are required. Consider a compact notepad example that fits the 400-word limit, since the example line format was useful but the notepad is easy to exceed across many players.

answers.confusing_rules: The interaction between swaps and the night-resolution order could be clearer. R20 says role-blocked actions are removed first, but also says swaps apply before anything else. R23 then describes redirected actions and says results name the player originally chosen. In play, I had to reason through what a Lookout would see if the watched target or a visitor was swapped, including whether the Smuggler would appear visiting both swapped players.
answers.missing_information: I had no essential information missing. The main thing that was hard to keep straight was the combination of claimed roles, actual visit evidence, and which Fabricator effects were still available: a visit identifies a destination, not the action, and framing does not reveal itself publicly.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to tell whether Carol's visit to Grace was a Katana attack or some other action. My Lookout result could only show the visitor, not their action; this is an intended information limit rather than an interface failure.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: I saw no clear mechanical bug. An oddity in the Day 2 discussion was that several players asked for Night 2 results before Night 2 had happened, even after others corrected them. This may reflect players losing track of the phase rather than a rules error.
answers.suggestions: Add a compact, searchable rules reference for visits, swaps, role-blocks, and attack/defense resolution. A phase-and-night timeline showing which nights have occurred, plus a concise table of public claims, flips, votes, and deaths, would help players avoid mixing claims with confirmed facts. Keep the distinction between a Lookout's observed visit and the action itself explicit in the result.

answers.confusing_rules: R22 speaking budget: the prompt gives a per-turn price table, but the exact budget carry-over and round multiplier (1x for rounds 1-3, then +0.5 per round) were hard to apply across a whole Day. The trial-only budget and free 150-word defense were only clear once a trial started. R4 says a nominee's last message comes after all others, but it's unclear whether the nominator's Yes counts in the nomination majority when the nominator is dead or a rig is active. Swap rules (R23) and Lookout or Tracker redirection were hard to reason about without seeing the swap, since a Lookout watching a swapped player watches the other player.
answers.missing_information: No running record of remaining speaking budget per player, so I could not judge who could afford long defenses or who was saving budget. The public ledger shows Private messages none yet, which made it unclear whether private messages were tracked at all. No visible record of each Yakuza's chosen Katana holder and target before the night resolved, so Yakuza vote splits were only visible after the fact. Trial vote totals are shown, but not which trial votes were Ballot Stuffer-doubled, which made the total-versus-revealed check hard to use.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to see the full Night 3 Seer and Sheriff claims cross-checked against the Lookout and Tracker data in one view, but the ledger only lists claims text, not structured results. I wanted to privately check Heidi and Niaj's claims with Judy, but there was no way to see whether private messages existed between them since the ledger reported none. I could not ask the moderator for a clarification on how the Ex-Con random visit is shown to a Lookout.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: The public ledger says Private messages sent: none yet even at the end of Day 4, which seems suspicious if Yakuza or other players used private chats; it may not be tracked. Dave's will (Sheriff, Mallory Evil) conflicted with his revealed Tracker role, which the game allowed without any mechanism to verify it; that's an intended forgery path but the forgery was only confirmed by the Fabricator's own night result, which was revealed too late to help. Carol's revealed Night 3 visit to Grace was the Katana attack visit, while her earlier claimed role was Vanilla, which is consistent with the mechanics, but the role-block claim of Party Animal could not be checked. Ivan's Ex-Con claim after nomination gave a plausible-looking alignment read that the game then ruled out only via the Katana holder reading Good, a mechanic that is easy to miss.
answers.suggestions: Show a structured public table of each night's visits and results (Lookout, Tracker, Seer pairs, Sheriff checks) so claims can be cross-checked without manual reading. Include remaining speaking budget per player in the public ledger. Make private message logging visible in the ledger with counts per Day, including Yakuza private chats where it's relevant. Clarify in R19 how a Katana holder's Good appearance interacts with Sheriff claims made before the holder is known. Consider a short rule summary per role in the prompt so players can check tokens and night actions without reading the whole rulebook.

answers.confusing_rules: The Seer's random-pair rule took effort to pin down: players who die that night count, and a chosen pair is a visit while the random pair is not. The Katana-versus-Standard-protection outcome had to be derived from the strictly-higher rule (equal Standard attack and defense fails). Medic self-protection token costs appear only in the prompt, not in the rules text. Day ending by a silent round versus speaking budget exhaustion was not clearly linked.
answers.missing_information: I could not see my current speaking budget or the trial-only budget in this summary, so I could not plan how much to say. The public ledger does not track who holds the Katana, the living Yakuza count, or remaining swap, vigilante and clerk tokens, so I had to reconstruct those from announcements. Private message contents are hidden, so the ledger's 'none yet' is hard to interpret.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted a clear way to send a private message to one player to test claims without it being public, but the turn format did not show a PM option. I also wanted to see the full visit history of other players across nights, which no role or summary gives me.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing clearly broken, but Day 2 became very repetitive, with many near-identical prompts and replies, so the discussion stalled without new information. Dave's will made a Sheriff claim that the moderator never marked as forged, so players had to infer forgery themselves. Conflicting Seer and Sheriff results on Dave were left unresolved for a full day, which made the early game hard to resolve.
answers.suggestions: Show a public per-night summary of visits (who visited whom, excluding private results) and the Katana holder at each Day start. Show a running count of living players per faction and remaining tokens for each role that has them. Show the speaking budget and remaining trial budget plainly at each turn. Offer an explicit pass option for nomination and message turns so silence is distinguishable from a considered choice.

answers.confusing_rules: 1) R19 doesn't say which wins when exceptions conflict, e.g. a Fabricator framing the Katana holder (Good vs Evil) or framing an Ex-Con. It didn't come up, but I had no rule to fall back on. 2) Night numbering confused players. Day 2 comes before Night 2, and the log labels nights as '[Day N night]'. On Day 2 many players kept asking Heidi and Grace for 'N2 results' that couldn't exist yet. 3) The Medic text implies Standard protection of others is free, but it is worded around spending tokens. I had to read 'spend 1 token to give Strong instead' as meaning the base protection costs nothing. 4) R23 has a Lookout's watch follow a swap. Several players correctly worked out that a Smuggler swap would have put Erin on Grace's visitor list, but the chain through R23 and the Smuggler text is subtle and easy to misapply. 5) R8 says each Yakuza learns what actions the others chose. It doesn't say whether a Yakuza who died that night still gets the summary.
answers.missing_information: As moderator I had to track a lot by hand: the current Katana holder and its moves, who was framed each night, whether a forged will was pending, token counts for every role, and the seating circle. The circle matters for Surveyor and Diviner groups and was never shown to me explicitly. There was also no single view combining 'actions submitted' with 'visits computed'. I built the visit graph mentally to answer Judy's Lookout watches and to apply Heidi's frame-affected checks. A per-night resolution table with visits, attack versus defense levels, appearances, and resulting messages would have reduced the risk of error.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted an automatic resolver or checklist that applies R20 in order and shows each step: role-blocks, swaps, visits, attacks, investigations, notifications. That way I could verify results such as Ivan reading Not Evil as Katana holder on N2, or Niaj's Standard protection blocking the Standard Katana, rather than computing them freehand. I also wanted a way to flag to players that a 'Night N' result refers to the night after Day N, to stop the repeated premature N2 requests.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: 1) Erin died on N3 to Alice's Vigilante shot but still received the Yakuza night summary and a 'You have 2 swap tokens' line. Sending results to a dead player is harmless but odd. 2) Yakuza summary formatting was inconsistent. On N3 Carol got the team summary folded into her personal result, while N1 and N2 had a separate shared summary. 3) Night result messages varied in style ('Night 2:' vs 'Night 2 result:', token counts sometimes given and sometimes omitted). 4) Ivan as Katana holder privately learned his attack FAILED, but the rules don't say whether the other Yakuza learn that. I didn't tell them, which seemed consistent with R8 (choices but not results). 5) Grace was killed on N3 and still received her random Seer pair. That is correct per R10, but worth confirming it's intended. I found no mechanical misresolution: the frames, Katana appearances, defense comparisons, Lookout lists and the final win check all matched the rules.
answers.suggestions: 1) Add an explicit precedence order to R19 for overlapping appearance effects. 2) Rename log phases to 'Night N (after Day N)' and have the program remind players on Day N that no Night N result exists yet. 3) Rewrite the Medic text: 'Standard protection on another player is free; 1 token makes it Strong; self-protection costs 1 more token.' 4) Give the moderator a state panel showing the Katana holder, active frames and forges, traps, Executioner targets, tokens and seating, plus an R20 step-by-step resolution view. 5) Stop sending night results to players who died that night, unless the result is meant for their will or the record. 6) Standardize result message templates across roles and nights.

title: Post-game lessons: tips players wish they'd known, and how past tips went

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: When a Sheriff or Seer result conflicts with a revealed role, first check whether the claimant could have been framed or swapped that night; a Fabricator frame plus forged will explains many contradictions, so don't treat one conflict as proof of a lie.

Track which Night 1 claims are conditional and demand the claimant's exact target and result each night in a fixed format; claims that shift wording between days (e.g. Seer 'non-Good' becoming 'Good or Neutral') are a strong tell.
Look for the lone No voters on a nomination that later gets flipped; a Yakuza who voted No early often reveals themselves, and the same teammates tend to vote No together.
Keep the Medic and Sheriff's pending actions private until after the night; publicly stating protection targets lets the Yakuza plan around them.
A Lookout's watch shows visits but not the purpose; a lone visitor to a Katana victim is strong, but check whether a Smuggler swap or a Party Animal block explains the visit before concluding.

tips_feedback.tip: A visit shows a destination, not an action: tracks and watches can't tell protection from framing or a Katana hit.
tips_feedback.why: Judy's Lookout watch on Grace showed only Carol visiting, and the Day 4 vote used that correctly while still weighing the swap alternative.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction in claims, votes or mechanical results.
tips_feedback.why: Votes on Ivan and Carol were tied to specific mismatches like the Ex-Con claim against Heidi's Not Evil result and the lone visit to Grace.

tips_feedback.tip: Get the mechanics right before calling a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat.
tips_feedback.why: Several players argued that Dave's Sheriff will contradicted his Tracker reveal, which was only a contradiction because the will was a false claim, and I avoided over-reading silence.

output.reason: Answering the retrospective lessons and tip feedback requested after the game ended.

notepad_before: D2 r4: Night 2 has not happened; Heidi and Grace have only N1 results. Heidi (Sheriff, Dave Evil) and Grace (Seer, Dave/Mallory differ) are consistent if Dave was framed and his will forged. Dave Tracker flip = Good. Dave's will calling me Evil is unverified. Carol, Erin, Frank, Ivan, Bob, Judy, Alice, Niaj: no trial case yet. Watch who pushes a trial on Heidi or Grace without N1 cross-checks. No nomination from me yet.
notepad_after: D2 r4: Night 2 has not happened; Heidi and Grace have only N1 results. Heidi (Sheriff, Dave Evil) and Grace (Seer, Dave/Mallory differ) are consistent if Dave was framed and his will forged. Dave Tracker flip = Good. Dave's will calling me Evil is unverified. Carol, Erin, Frank, Ivan, Bob, Judy, Alice, Niaj: no trial case yet. Watch who pushes a trial on Heidi or Grace without N1 cross-checks. No nomination from me yet.

lessons.tip: Before the team commits a Katana attack, check whether the target is a Medic who can self-protect; a Standard hit on a Medic with a token fails, so pick targets whose protection is already spent or unknown.

Avoid unnecessary Yakuza-chat agreement loops that just repeat 'Ready'; instead settle the holder, target and swap decision once with a single confirmed vote per member to save budget and avoid stale plans.
A fake Vanilla claim is fragile when a teammate later flips a different role; if your team member is a real active role, claim it early with a consistent result set rather than denying it.
When a player votes No on a nomination and then Guilty after hearing the defense, that shift is only a weak lead; compare the reasons given against the mechanical evidence before voting.
A Lookout's visitor list on a victim is strong evidence, but check whether the visitor could be a Smuggler swap or a Party Animal role-block before treating it as proof of a Katana attack.

tips_feedback.tip: Bus a doomed teammate with Yes and Guilty. But first do the vote math in night chat.

tips_feedback.why: Ivan's Ex-Con claim was contradicted by Heidi's Not Evil result, and Carol's late Party Animal claim was also suspect, so the fake claims became the town's case.

tips_feedback.tip: Never put team plans in daytime PMs and don't PM teammates on Day 1.
tips_feedback.why: No private messages were sent, so the team's plans stayed hidden from Eavesdroppers and Wiretaps.

tips_feedback.tip: Give the Katana to a low-value member with a cover story ready, and move it the same night a Lookout or Tracker names the holder.
tips_feedback.why: Moving the Katana to Ivan on Night 2 made him the visible visitor to Heidi, and the Lookout's watch exposed him on Day 3.

Post your own night target and visit in your first speech after the night, before the conflict escalates; players who keep deferring their visit info look like they are hiding a visit.

Once a Yakuza is hanged, expect the remaining Yakuza to mirror the same vote; track which players voted No with the flipped members and check their next-night actions against those votes.

tips_feedback.why: Tracking who voted No alongside Ivan and Carol helped focus the trial pressure on the bloc and eventually exposed Carol.

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: Self-protection with Standard costs 1 token, and a Standard protection on a Standard attacker is a guaranteed save; repeated free protection on the same target is predictable, so vary between protecting likely Katana targets and self-protecting when the Katana holder is Yakuza.

Before accepting a Lookout visit as proof of an attack, check the visitor's claimed role for a random or automatic visit (Ex-Con) and whether a Yakuza could have swapped; a single visitor list is strong but not conclusive.
Ask Sheriff and Seer claimants to post results on the night they happen and cross-check pairs against Lookout watches early; conflicting pair or check claims in the same Day waste the trial time.
A No vote on a nomination that later flips to Guilty after a claim change is a strong read on the voter; track who voted No with known Yakuza, since that cluster was the decisive signal.

Claiming a fresh active role after being nominated (Vanilla to Ex-Con or Party Animal) made the team look guilty; claim a role before the nomination, and keep the claim consistent with visits the Lookout can see.

tips_feedback.tip: Map early PM clusters and co-nominations; require votes or a mechanical result before hanging on a PM link.
tips_feedback.why: There were no private messages this game, so the mechanical results (Lookout watch, Katana survival, Seer pair) drove the trials, and I hanged only on checkable evidence.

tips_feedback.tip: After a Yakuza flips, top suspects are those who voted No on their nomination, voted Innocent when it could have saved them, or PM'd them.
tips_feedback.why: Carol, Erin and Ivan all voted No on Ivan's nomination, and this cluster pointed to the Yakuza team and Carol correctly.

tips_feedback.tip: Investigators and Medics: never announce tonight's target publicly or by PM.

lessons.tip: When a Sheriff or Seer result conflicts with a revealed role, first check whether the claimant could have been framed or swapped that night; a Fabricator frame plus forged will explains many contradictions, so don't treat one conflict as proof of a lie.

Track which Night 1 claims are conditional and demand the claimant's exact target and result each night in a fixed format; claims that shift wording between days (e.g. Seer 'non-Good' becoming 'Good or Neutral') are a strong tell.
Look for the lone No voters on a nomination that later gets flipped; a Yakuza who voted No early often reveals themselves, and the same teammates tend to vote No together.
Keep the Medic and Sheriff's pending actions private until after the night; publicly stating protection targets lets the Yakuza plan around them.
A Lookout's watch shows visits but not the purpose; a lone visitor to a Katana victim is strong, but check whether a Smuggler swap or a Party Animal block explains the visit before concluding.

tips_feedback.tip: A visit shows a destination, not an action: tracks and watches can't tell protection from framing or a Katana hit.
tips_feedback.why: Judy's Lookout watch on Grace showed only Carol visiting, and the Day 4 vote used that correctly while still weighing the swap alternative.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction in claims, votes or mechanical results.
tips_feedback.why: Votes on Ivan and Carol were tied to specific mismatches like the Ex-Con claim against Heidi's Not Evil result and the lone visit to Grace.

tips_feedback.tip: Get the mechanics right before calling a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat.
tips_feedback.why: Several players argued that Dave's Sheriff will contradicted his Tracker reveal, which was only a contradiction because the will was a false claim, and I avoided over-reading silence.

lessons.tip: Self-protection with Standard costs 1 token, and a Standard protection on a Standard attacker is a guaranteed save; repeated free protection on the same target is predictable, so vary between protecting likely Katana targets and self-protecting when the Katana holder is Yakuza.

Before accepting a Lookout visit as proof of an attack, check the visitor's claimed role for a random or automatic visit (Ex-Con) and whether a Yakuza could have swapped; a single visitor list is strong but not conclusive.
Ask Sheriff and Seer claimants to post results on the night they happen and cross-check pairs against Lookout watches early; conflicting pair or check claims in the same Day waste the trial time.
A No vote on a nomination that later flips to Guilty after a claim change is a strong read on the voter; track who voted No with known Yakuza, since that cluster was the decisive signal.

Claiming a fresh active role after being nominated (Vanilla to Ex-Con or Party Animal) made the team look guilty; claim a role before the nomination, and keep the claim consistent with visits the Lookout can see.

tips_feedback.tip: Map early PM clusters and co-nominations; require votes or a mechanical result before hanging on a PM link.
tips_feedback.why: There were no private messages this game, so the mechanical results (Lookout watch, Katana survival, Seer pair) drove the trials, and I hanged only on checkable evidence.

tips_feedback.tip: After a Yakuza flips, top suspects are those who voted No on their nomination, voted Innocent when it could have saved them, or PM'd them.
tips_feedback.why: Carol, Erin and Ivan all voted No on Ivan's nomination, and this cluster pointed to the Yakuza team and Carol correctly.

tips_feedback.tip: Investigators and Medics: never announce tonight's target publicly or by PM.
tips_feedback.why: I kept my protection targets private until results were public, which limited the Pharmacist and Katana holder's information; the Katana still hit Grace, a Seer who had announced her pair.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep Serial Killers and Arsonists in the pool after Yakuza die.
tips_feedback.why: Not relevant this game: no Neutral player existed, so the tip did not affect any decision and does not match this setup.

summary: Village won cleanly 9-0 against the Yakuza. Carol, Erin and Ivan all hid behind Vanilla claims on Day 1, but their night play gave them away. N1: Dave refused to claim, which made him stand out as a power role. Carol framed and killed him, then forged his will as 'Sheriff: Mallory Evil'. Dave flipped Tracker, so the will was exposed as a forgery at once. Heidi then reasoned out loud that Dave had been framed, and the town never mislynched Mallory. N2: the Yakuza moved the Katana to Ivan and sent it at the claimed Sheriff Heidi. Niaj's protection saved her, Judy's Lookout watch on Heidi saw Ivan visit, and Heidi's check on Ivan read Not Evil. Ivan switched mid-trial to an Ex-Con claim, which Heidi's Not Evil result contradicted, and he was hanged 10-1. Carol and Erin had voted No on his nomination, alongside Ivan himself. That vote, plus Grace's Bob/Erin 'different' pair, gave Alice a solid reason for a Basic Vigilante shot that killed Erin N3. That same night Carol killed the unprotected Grace (Niaj had protected Heidi again). Judy was watching Grace and saw Carol as the only visitor. Carol's swap excuse, then a late Party Animal claim, failed, and she was hanged. Erin went the whole game without using either of her two swap tokens, which was the Yakuza's biggest wasted resource.

lessons.tip: When forging a will, don't give the victim a specific role claim you can't confirm. Their real role is revealed with the will, and any mismatch tells the town a Fabricator exists and voids the will's accusation. Either forge something vague that fits many roles, or save the token for a victim whose role you've worked out.
lessons.evidence: Carol forged Dave's will as 'Sheriff: checked Mallory, Evil'. Dave flipped Tracker, and every player immediately called the will forged. Heidi and Judy used it to explain the frame, so Mallory was never put in danger.

lessons.tip: Assume a claimed investigator is being watched by a Lookout and protected by the Medic. Don't send a visible Katana holder straight at them. A Smuggler swap can redirect the attack or the watch, and Smugglers who hoard their tokens throw away the team's best defense against Lookouts.
lessons.evidence: N2: Ivan carried the Katana to Heidi, who was protected by Niaj and watched by Judy. N3: Carol went to Grace while Judy was watching. Both holders were seen and hanged. Erin died holding 2 unused swap tokens.

lessons.tip: Watch the player the Yakuza most want dead, which is the freshly claimed investigator. A watch on the night's Katana victim names the holder outright.
lessons.evidence: Judy watched the claimed Sheriff on N2 and saw Ivan. She watched the claimed Seer on N3 and saw only Carol. Those two reports decided both Yakuza hangings.

lessons.tip: When a teammate's nomination is clearly going to pass, vote Yes with the town. A No vote that saves no one ties you to the teammate once they flip.
lessons.evidence: Carol and Erin voted No on Ivan's 8-Yes nomination, then Guilty. After Ivan flipped Grunt, Frank and Heidi pointed at Carol's No vote, and Alice shot Erin, who had voted No and was also in Grace's 'different' pair.

lessons.tip: Choose a cover claim that explains possible visits and fits results already public. Don't switch claims mid-trial to a role that an existing check contradicts. Agree a cover action in night chat before you visit.
lessons.evidence: Ivan went from Vanilla to Ex-Con, but Heidi's Not Evil result was impossible for an Ex-Con and matched a Katana holder. Carol went from Vanilla to a swap excuse to Party Animal. Each change made the town more sure, not less.

lessons.tip: After a successful-looking protection, expect the Yakuza to switch targets. Rotate between the claimed investigators, or self-protect once claimed, rather than repeating the same predictable protection.
lessons.evidence: Niaj protected Heidi on N2 (she survived the Katana) and again on N3. The Yakuza switched to Grace, who was unprotected and died.

lessons.tip: When a Good flip clashes with an Evil alignment result, treat it as evidence of a Fabricator frame rather than evidence that the investigator is lying. Also re-derive what any paired Seer result means, since the frame changes how the paired player read.
lessons.evidence: Heidi's 'Dave Evil' plus Dave's Tracker flip proved a frame. Grace corrected her 'Mallory non-Good' reading, and the town avoided hanging the framed Mallory on Day 2.

lessons.tip: On Day 1, a quiet Vanilla-style claim or plain cooperation is safer than flatly refusing to claim. A visible refusal marks you as a power role for the first Katana.
lessons.evidence: Dave refused to claim despite repeated asks, became the focus of the day, and was the Yakuza's N1 target.

tips_feedback.tip: A visit shows a destination, not an action... A corroborated Lookout's lone other visitor to a victim is near-proof.
tips_feedback.why: The town treated Judy's sole-visitor reports (Ivan to Heidi, Carol to Grace) as near-proof and hanged both Yakuza correctly. Frank, Heidi and Judy also pointed out that Carol's swap excuse didn't fit, because a Smuggler swap would have shown Erin as a visitor.

tips_feedback.tip: After a Yakuza flips, top suspects are those who voted No on their nomination...
tips_feedback.why: Ivan's Grunt flip made the Carol/Erin No votes a lead. Frank opened Day 4 with it, and it backed up Alice's Vigilante target.

tips_feedback.tip: The Katana holder reads Not Evil that night, so a Not Evil result clears nothing; say so when posting.
tips_feedback.why: Heidi posted Ivan's Not Evil with this caveat. The town then saw that Ivan's Ex-Con claim (which reads Evil) couldn't explain it, while holding the Katana could.

tips_feedback.tip: Shoot only on a mechanical lead... Use Basic shots.
tips_feedback.why: Alice held fire until she had Grace's Bob/Erin pair and Erin's No vote on Ivan. Her Basic shot then killed the Smuggler with only one token spent.

tips_feedback.tip: Protect likely Katana targets, analysts then claimed investigators. Once you've claimed Medic, self-protect with a token instead of repeating a predictable protection.
tips_feedback.why: Protecting the claimed Sheriff on N2 saved Heidi and gave the town the failed-attack lead. On N3 Niaj repeated the same protection instead of varying it, and Grace died, so the second half of the tip was ignored.

tips_feedback.tip: Bus a doomed teammate with Yes and Guilty... Futile lone Innocents hang you later.
tips_feedback.why: Carol and Erin bussed Ivan on the trial vote but voted No on a nomination that was clearly going to pass. That partial deviation became the town's case against them, which shows the advice holds.

issues.description: On Day 2 (after only Night 1), many players (Bob, Frank, Erin, Ivan, Niaj, and Mallory at first) repeatedly asked Heidi and Grace for their 'Night 2' targets and results. Erin asked Grace whether she 'also paired anyone on Night 2'. Mallory, Grace and Heidi each pointed out that Night 2 hadn't happened yet, but players kept asking. This suggests the Day N / Night N-1 numbering isn't clear enough in the prompt or state shown to players.

Mallory said on Day 2 that 'Dave's Tracker flip doesn't prove Dave was Good'. Tracker is a Village role, and a revealed role shows the player's true alignment, so the flip does prove it. Several players corrected her.
In the Night 3 Yakuza chat, Carol claimed Niaj (Medic) 'can't protect himself'. The Medic role allows self-protection for 1 token (2 for Strong). Erin correctly pointed out the mistake.

Several Day 2 inferences from Grace's differing Dave/Mallory pair ignored the Neutral possibility (e.g. Judy and Frank said a framed Dave makes Mallory Good, not Good or Neutral). Grace herself first called Mallory non-Good, then corrected it. Each claim was later fixed, but alignment-comparison logic caused repeated confusion.
